"Implement the solution in src/main/java/SimpleLinkedList.java so that the tests in src/test/java/SimpleLinkedListTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Write a prototype of the music player application.

For the prototype, each song will simply be represented by a number.
Given a range of numbers (the song IDs), create a singly linked list.

Given a singly linked list, you should be able to reverse the list to play the songs in the opposite order.

~~~~exercism/note
The linked list is a fundamental data structure in computer science, often used in the implementation of other data structures.

The simplest kind of linked list is a **singly** linked list.
That means that each element (or \"node\") contains data, along with something that points to the next node in the list.

If you want to dig deeper into linked lists, check out [this article][intro-linked-list] that explains it using nice drawings.

[intro-linked-list]: https://medium.com/basecs/whats-a-linked-list-anyway-part-1-d8b7e6508b9d
~~~~


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

content.text: First, let's check the test files and the project structure.

The test file is in the default package (no package declaration). The solution file is also in the default package. Implement a singly linked list.

Note: `push` adds to the front (head). `pop` removes from the head. `reverse` reverses. `asArray` returns the list in order from head to tail (in the test, pushing 9,8,7,6,5 gives head=5, so it becomes {'5','6','7','8','9'}).

Constructor from array: values are pushed in order.
Next, I'll run the tests. Let me check the build system.

All 7 tests pass. I implemented `SimpleLinkedList` in src/main/java/SimpleLinkedList.java as a singly linked list:

- **`Node<T>`** — a private static inner class holding a value and a `next` pointer (the only helper, kept inside the solution file per the constraints).
- **`push(T)`** — prepends a new node at the head, so the most recently pushed element is popped first.
- **`pop()`** — removes and returns the head, throwing `NoSuchElementException` on an empty list.
- **`reverse()`** — reverses the `next` pointers in place, so `pop` after reversing yields elements in the original push order.
- **`asArray(Class<T>)`** — walks head to tail into an array created via `Array.newInstance`, returning an empty array for an empty list.
- **`size()`** — tracks the count with an integer field; the `T[]` constructor pushes each value in sequence.
